set.approach: Begin from the little parking spot where the Rock Creek drainage opens out, and cross the small diversion dam. There is no trail beyond: expect bushwhacking and sidehilling, and the right-hand side of the drainage is the quicker way. After several hours a large rock tower stands below the face, and it can be passed on the right (easier) or the left (shorter but steeper).
set.descent_text: The route reaches a notch on the northwest ridge, and easy scrambling then leads to the summit. From the summit, follow the standard ridge trail most of the way down. At a notch with a tree, leave the trail and go right, then travel cross-country northwest back to the mouth of the Rock Creek drainage.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; a trip report confirms the standard southwest ridge as the descent from the summit.

set.approach: Two ways lead to the base of the north face. One follows the standard route up the neighbouring peak past the ridge crux to the saddle below its final climb, then drops east from the north end of the saddle over scree or snow until below the face; the east slope has short cliff bands and is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast. The other starts at the west fork trailhead at the end of the forest road in the Pahsimeroi valley, climbs the hillside west of the road to the cliff bands on the east ridge, and passes two lakes to reach the face. Broken Wings starts by climbing the snow slope below the line to a cave at the foot of the first chimney.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the ridge rather than the summit. Traverse west along the ridge to the junction with the neighbouring peak, then either follow its trail down or take a steep snow ramp east back into the canyon. Check the avalanche forecast before using the snow ramp.

review.notes: Route page: snow slope to cave, ridge traverse west, trail or east snow ramp. Area page: both approaches. AAJ note confirms line ends on the ridge/North Peak, not the summit.

set.descent_text: From the top, downclimb the fourth-class ridge to the end of the ridge crux on the neighbouring peak's trail. Follow the trail up to just before the final climb from the saddle, then drop east from the end of the saddle to stay clear of the cliff bands and return to the base of the face. Be wary of avalanche conditions on that east slope and check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent; area page gives approaches and east-slope hazard; guide page confirms line from base to steep snow near summit.

set.descent_text: Walk off the east side after topping out.

set.approach: The south-side walls rise straight from flat fields beside the highway, and a pull-out east of the Gap leaves only a short walk. The route takes the little triangular buttress that sits west of the Alpine Simulator one, with a snow couloir on each side, and lies right of Fear Machine. A creek and thick willows lie below the face; cross them to reach the slab ramp that leads to the steeper second pitch.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the east from the top.

review.notes: Route page: location and walk-off east. Trip report: short approach from pull-out and east-side walk-off terrain on the same side of the Gap.

set.approach: From the town of Carcross, head south along the highway to the campground and park on the roadside at the main entrance or across from the trailhead opposite. Walk the unplowed campground road down to the lake, then ski or snowshoe across toward the obvious ice flows. Both the approach and the climbs are avalanche terrain, and the snowpack is thin and faceted, so check the avalanche forecast and carry rescue gear. Solar Flare is the flow to the left of Soleil.

review.notes: Area page for approach and hazards; route page for position. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the signed side road to Kathleen Lake, south of Haines Junction. Every climb here requires crossing the lake, so make sure the ice is safe first. Beyond the lake the approach is long, usually on skis or a sled, and the slopes on the way in are major avalanche terrain; check the avalanche forecast. Blue Nun is the right-hand of the two lines at the Nuns, shorter and steeper than Flying Nun.

review.notes: Area page for access; route pages for position. No descent stated.

set.approach: The route can be seen from the road. Pull off beside Tushi Lake on its west shore, toward the southern end. The way to the base is a steep gully, and the approach is the hard part: assess avalanche conditions first and check the avalanche forecast. The gully can have rock steps, so in lean snow years expect some mixed climbing, and there are many overhead hazards.

review.notes: Single route page for the approach. No descent stated.

set.approach: Heading south out of Micaville on NC 80, take two right turns onto the side roads that reach the Woody Ridge trailhead. Follow the Woody Ridge Trail up the logging-road switchbacks, then leave it and head north on old flat logging roads that cross springs and streams, including two major creeks. The road ends at the second major crossing. A faint trail then climbs beside the stream; stay close to the creek until a low waterfall blocks it; that is the start of the route.
set.descent_text: Walk and rappel the route, rappelling after the steep opening pitch.

review.notes: Two route pages share the approach; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Heading south out of Micaville on NC 80, take two right turns onto the side roads that reach the Woody Ridge trailhead. Follow the Woody Ridge Trail up the logging-road switchbacks, then leave it and head north on old flat logging roads that cross springs and streams, including two major creeks. The road ends at the second major crossing. A faint trail climbs beside the stream to the waterfall on the Brown's Creek line. Crescent begins around the back of the rock buttress on the left side of that creek.
set.descent_text: Descend the Woody Ridge Trail, following it across the rock step near the top.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms access roads off NC 80.

set.approach: Use the Woody Ridge approach roads to the end of the road where Crescent and Y Gully start, then follow the gravel road and the drainage beyond. Eventually bear left into the large drainage north of Locust Ridge. The route lies south of Y Gully and splits near its end like it.
set.descent_text: On top, join the Black Mountain Crest Trail going south, then go down the Colbert Ridge Trail to where it meets the road. A second car left there saves the walk back to the start.

review.notes: Route page; area page for road access.

set.approach: The route is easily climbed but not easily reached, and the best access is along the Buncombe Horse Trail. Expect a long bushwhack and carry a map, compass and altimeter.
set.descent_text: The best way down is the Buncombe Horse Trail, the same way you came in.

review.notes: Single route page; no distances used.

set.approach: On the Buncombe Horse Trail off the forest road, hike a short way, then turn right (west) onto hunter trails and follow them into the Middle Creek drainage. At the base of the crux you can climb directly or traverse right to the other variation.
set.descent_text: On top, join the Black Mountain Crest Trail going north across the summit of Cattail Peak, then go down the Colbert Ridge Trail to where it meets the road. A second car left there saves the walk back.

review.notes: Single route page; distances omitted.

set.approach: Park at the Buncombe Horse trailhead and hike the Buncombe Horse Trail a long way, until it reaches the lower open flanks of Maple Camp Bald. Turn left there and bushwhack to the creek, then climb the two ice pitches in the creek until it meets the trail again.
set.descent_text: Rejoin the trail at the top of the creek and hike it back to the trailhead.

review.notes: Single route page; mileage omitted.

set.approach: Start as for Brown's Creek Falls and continue past the steep ice pitch up the gully above it, over a succession of lower-angle slabs and steps to a broad rounded basin where the gully ends.
set.descent_text: Leave the gully by the slabs on the left or centre into dense rhododendron, then head up and left into a rocky gully within it that leads to the Woody Ridge Trail. Expect a short steep bushwhack.

review.notes: Route page for the gully and exit; Brown's Creek Falls page for the shared approach.

set.approach: Park at the Woody Ridge trailhead and walk the logging roads toward Crescent. A short way along, turn left and follow the creek up, then continue up the slope to where the ice ends, just beyond the crux pitch. In snowy conditions the right side of the Y is the preferred finish.
set.descent_text: Reaching the ridge, locate the Black Mountain Crest Trail, go north along it to the Woody Ridge Trail, and take that back to the car.

review.notes: Single route page; descent stated on it.

set.approach: Drive east on NM 38 up the canyon from Questa. Past the first buttress, dozens of slabs and outcrops line the canyon; the route is high on the south side above the highway, opposite the mine, and reached by a long hike up steep talus.

review.notes: Area page, AAJ and route page agree on location; no descent stated.

set.approach: Drive east on NM 38 up the canyon from Questa. The route is on the north side of the highway by the first rock buttress on the left, only a few paces off the road.

set.approach: From the town of Truchas, a network of dirt roads leads up the creek valley to the trailhead for the Rio Quemado trail. The trail reaches the falls, and skis with skins are recommended in most snow. The line goes up the middle of the falls on stair-stepped ice, the easiest route on them.
set.descent_text: Trees above the falls serve as anchors. After topping out, either leave webbing on them or walk around the north side of the falls.

review.notes: Area page for approach, route page for line and descent.

set.approach: Take the Piedra Lisa trail and cross Waterfall Canyon a short way along it. An unmaintained track follows the streambed up to the falls; you can swap some of it for the ridgeline either side and drop into the canyon, though that is also a bushwhack. At the first cliff section scramble up and right.

review.notes: Area and route pages agree; distances omitted. No descent stated.
